role: The boot problem, precisely, with a decision. Proposed as a new top-level 'boot' key on esp-soc's chips/esp32c3.json rather than a competing chip file -- not merged into that file directly to avoid a concurrent write against another agent's in-progress artifact in a shared scratchpad.
verified: 2026-08-24, every quoted line below fetched from the pinned tag via raw.githubusercontent.com.

three_stages.what_it_touches: Runs at reset from a fixed address inside the 384KB on-die mask ROM (0x40000000, per esp-soc's memory map, size 0x60000). Samples GPIO_STRAP_REG to decide UART-download-mode vs SPI-boot. On SPI-boot it arms BOTH watchdogs' flashboot-protection mode (confirmed indirectly and precisely: bootloader_init.c's bootloader_config_wdt(), the FIRST watchdog-touching code in the 2nd-stage bootloader, opens with the comment 'At this point, the flashboot protection of RWDT and MWDT0 will have been automatically enabled' -- 'automatically' here means by the mask ROM, since nothing in the 2nd-stage bootloader's own earlier code enables them) with a short timeout, reads the 2nd-stage bootloader image from flash offset 0x0 (ESP_PRIMARY_BOOTLOADER_OFFSET), copies it into IRAM/DRAM, and jumps to call_start_cpu0 in that image. It does NOT set up the flash-cache MMU or parse a partition table -- that is entirely the 2nd stage's job.
three_stages.why_it_cannot_be_fully_skipped: The mask ROM is not only a boot-time actor -- it is a permanent, always-present function library. Both the 2nd-stage bootloader and the app link directly against ROM-resident symbols via esp32c3.rom.ld (memcpy/memset variants, esp_rom_printf, SPI-flash primitives, and load-bearing for the clock work already verified here: esp_rom_delay_us(), which components/esp_hw_support/port/esp32c3/rtc_clk.c calls repeatedly for every RTC-domain clock switch -- see rtc_cntl-contract.json's clock_select_findings). A CALL instruction to a fixed mask-ROM address exists in the compiled app binary regardless of when in the app's lifetime it executes, not only during the boot handoff. Skip the mask ROM's address range entirely and the very first esp_rom_delay_us() call -- which happens before app_main(), inside rtc_clk_init() -- is a jump into unmapped memory.

three_stages.what_it_touches: components/bootloader_support/src/esp32c3/bootloader_esp32c3.c:125 bootloader_init(), in exact order, quoted: bootloader_hardware_init() -> bootloader_ana_reset_config() -> bootloader_super_wdt_auto_feed() [silences the fourth, analog Super WDT -- see rtc_cntl-contract.json] -> bootloader_init_mem()+clear bss -> bootloader_clock_configure() [rtc_clk_init, includes the TIMG_RTCCALICFG calibration loop] -> bootloader_console_init() -> bootloader_init_ext_mem() [cache+MMU init] -> bootloader_flash_update_id() -> bootloader_flash_xmc_startup() -> bootloader_read_bootloader_header()+bootloader_check_bootloader_validity() [compares chip revision against efuse, matches esp-soc's EFUSE stub note about min_chip_rev_full] -> bootloader_init_spi_flash() -> bootloader_check_wdt_reset() -> bootloader_config_wdt() [disables RWDT+MWDT0 flashboot protection -- see rtc_cntl-contract.json WDT_FLASHBOOT_MOD_EN] -> bootloader_enable_random(). Then bootloader_start.c's call_start_cpu0(): load partition table -> select_partition_number() -> bootloader_utility_load_boot_image(). Everything here is deterministic given the flash image bytes: same input always produces the same selected partition, the same app-image load addresses, and the same final WDT/cache state.
three_stages.why_it_can_be_skipped: Because that determinism is exactly the property a host-side (Python) loader can precompute once, ahead of execution, from static analysis of the .bin/partition-table -- the same reasoning this project already applies elsewhere (RP2040 UF2 loading, docs/architectures.md 5.3, is explicitly preferred over emulating the RP2040 boot ROM's own USB-flashing protocol). Re-running partition-table parsing, image-header validation, and flash-cache-window arithmetic inside the emulator on every boot buys nothing: it is not part of what the app under test exercises, it has no equivalent on the RP2040/STM32 paths already chosen, and skipping it removes the largest single chunk of ESP-IDF-internal C code (bootloader_support, ~dozens of files) from the emulation surface entirely.

three_stages.what_it_touches: The app's own cpu_start.c (not fetched this session -- out of scope for this deliverable, but same function name call_start_cpu0 in a different translation unit) runs esp_system startup: brownout, watchdog reconfiguration (RWDT is typically re-armed here under IDF's own task-watchdog/interrupt-watchdog scheme, now fed by the FreeRTOS idle task rather than by the bootloader), rtc_clk_init() runs a SECOND time in the app context (the same TIMG_RTCCALICFG loop, now for the app's own clock configuration, possibly at a different target frequency than the bootloader used), heap init, FreeRTOS scheduler start, and eventually app_main() runs as a FreeRTOS task.

decision.question: Emulate from the mask ROM, or load the app directly and skip both mask ROM and 2nd-stage bootloader?
decision.survey_view_being_tested: docs/architectures.md 4.1 states 'You can skip the bootloader; you cannot skip the ROM' without further elaboration on where exactly the line falls or what crossing it costs.
decision.answer: Confirmed, and sharpened to something concrete enough to implement: RUN THE REAL MASK ROM (as a loaded binary, executed for real by the core), SKIP the 2nd-stage bootloader's C code (replicate its side effects statically instead), LOAD the app image directly.
reasoning: The mask ROM must be present as real, executable content -- not stubbed, not reimplemented function-by-function -- because app code calls into it at arbitrary points during normal operation (esp_rom_delay_us above is the concrete, already-verified example), not only at the boot handoff. Trapping every individual ROM export as a native callback is an open-ended, ongoing surface (every future firmware sample can call a ROM function nobody has trapped yet); loading the real ROM image and executing it is closed and exactly matches silicon.

This is not hypothetical extra work: espressif/esp-rom-elfs (github.com/espressif/esp-rom-elfs, license verified Apache-2.0 by fetching its actual LICENSE file text, not just repository metadata) publishes exactly these ROM images, and a file named pic_esp32c3-rom.bin already exists in this session's shared scratchpad -- almost certainly extracted by a prior agent from the PICSimLab NOGUI AppImage that docs/architectures.md section 7 already confirmed bundles the ESP ROM images. The dependency this decision needs is already sitting in the workspace; provenance of that specific file was not re-verified by this agent and should be confirmed before relying on it.

The 2nd-stage bootloader's C code, by contrast, is safe to skip WHOLESALE because its entire job is deterministic given the flash image -- see 'why_it_can_be_skipped' above -- with the load-bearing caveat that its two watchdog SIDE EFFECTS must still be replayed statically before app code runs, or the app inherits an armed RWDT flashboot-protect window and a Super WDT with no software escape at all: (a) RTC_CNTL_WDTCONFIG0.WDT_FLASHBOOT_MOD_EN must start cleared (not left at its own reset-value 1) -- equivalent to bootloader_config_wdt()'s effect; (b) RTC_CNTL_SWD_CONF.SWD_AUTO_FEED_EN must start SET -- equivalent to bootloader_super_wdt_auto_feed()'s effect, quoted in full in rtc_cntl-contract.json. Both are one-line harness-side pokes applied before the app's entry point runs, not a watchdog model.

The flash-cache MMU window (0x42000000 exec / 0x3C000000 rodata, per esp-soc's memory map) that the 2nd-stage bootloader would normally program from the app image's own segment headers can be set up the same static way: the host loader reads the app image header once (same .bin the real bootloader would have validated) and tells the harness where each IROM/DROM segment lives, matching esp-soc's own chip-file note under irom_cache/drom_cache ('the loader statically serves app-image bytes at their vaddrs, standing in for the cache MMU') -- this decision is consistent with, not a departure from, esp-soc's existing memory-map file.
decision.what_is_NOT_resolved_by_this_agent: Efuse chip-revision matching (bootloader_check_bootloader_validity, esp-soc's EFUSE stub note) still gates whether a real app IMAGE HEADER's min_chip_rev_full check passes even after skipping the bootloader code that normally performs it -- if the loader skips validation entirely rather than replicating its pass/fail outcome, an app built expecting a revision check to have happened could behave differently than on hardware. Left as an open question for whoever implements the loader, not resolved here.
